bottom-skirt-plum.finding: the 24 px FIT-6v2 strip (x 623–628, y 990–996) is the hem's rounded right corner meeting the thigh: the generated picture draws the same thigh contour at the same place (C's outer thigh x 627–628, the picture's x 627–628); 22 of 24 px show skin or contour in the picture too, 2–3 px are the extraction's antialiased hem edge. The fabric must NOT hide it (it is the leg below the hem) and the item is not too narrow. The piece is 6 × 7 px — one pixel over FIT-6v2's crossing allowance (≤ 6 × 6), which is why it counts as a strip. FIT-4 9 px is D-207's recorded check artefact (a 1 px side-seam column next to the arm–torso gap). Under the unchanged gates the skirt stays technically rejected; changing a gate is an owner decision and is not made here.
